timing: Written after the first v1 diagnostic outcomes were computed and inspected; post-hoc reporting clarification
reason: An unmatched alarm under one-to-one matching can be either a repeat notification within a labelled bump interval or an alarm outside any bump interval. Calling both a non-bump false alarm would conflate different engineering costs
unchanged: All v1 outcomes, selected candidates, event boundaries, tolerances, hard predictions, matching, denominators and primary unmatched-notification rates are retained; no threshold tuning or refitting

additional_outputs.nonbump_alarm_clusters: Alarm clusters having no eligible edge to any evaluable annotation interval at the stated tolerance
additional_outputs.duplicate_event_alarm_clusters: Unmatched alarm clusters having at least one eligible event edge; redundant event-associated notifications under the one-to-one rule
additional_outputs.rate_nonbump_alarms_per_nonbump_hour: nonbump_alarm_clusters / same explicit non-bump exposure hours

interpretation: Original unmatched count measures total excess notification burden, not only false-positive notifications on non-bump intervals. Added categorization is descriptive and is not a new confirmatory improvement criterion
